The cumulative frequency of MAPK pathway alterations in post-hormonal therapy HR+/HER2- tumors is 24.3% (171 out of 705 tumors).

This was determined by analyzing 23 canonical RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK pathway genes (including KRAS, HRAS, NRAS, BRAF, RAF1, ARAF, MAP2K1, MAP2K2, MAPK1, MAPK3, EGFR, SOS1, NF1, NF2, MAP3K1, MAP3K13, MAP3K14, DUSP4, RIT1, RRAS, RRAS2, RASA1, and SPRED1) across somatic mutations and copy-number aberrations (amplifications and deep deletions) in a cohort of 705 HR+/HER2- breast cancer samples collected after hormonal therapy exposure (metastatic sites and post-treatment primaries), compared against 657 treatment-naive HR+/HER2- primaries as reference.

Breakdown by alteration type:
- Mutations only: 134 samples (19.0%)
- Copy-number aberrations only: 51 samples (7.2%)
- Both mutation and CNA: 14 samples (2.0%)
- Any MAPK alteration: 171 samples (24.3%)

The most significantly enriched gene is NF1, with loss-of-function mutations in 5.2% of post-treatment tumors versus 1.5% of treatment-naive tumors (OR = 3.58, Fisher's exact p = 0.0002). RASA1 mutations are also significantly enriched (OR = 7.53, p = 0.040). Canonical oncogene hotspots are present at lower frequency: BRAF V600E (0.14%), KRAS G12 missense mutations (0.7%), and EGFR missense (1.1%). The overall MAPK alteration enrichment shows a trend toward significance (OR = 1.29, p = 0.059) compared to treatment-naive tumors (19.9%).

The dominant mechanism of MAPK activation in the endocrine-resistant setting is loss of negative regulators (NF1, RASA1), rather than activating oncogene mutations. NF1 loss removes RAS-GAP activity, causing constitutive RAS-MAPK signaling independent of estrogen receptor cross-talk, representing a plausible genomic mechanism of endocrine therapy resistance.
